newsitem.title: UK: UK Q3 cocoa grind seen flat to 10 pct up.
newsitem.headline: UK Q3 cocoa grind seen flat to 10 pct up.

text.p: UK third quarter cocoa grindings will be unchanged to as much as 10 percent up on last year's 34,400 tonnes, analysts said.
"We are expecting a 10 percent rise year-on-year in cocoa grindings in the third quarter," one said.
The forecast was based on perceptions of a general upturn in cocoa demand, aided by a milder summer and brisk exports.
"This summer was less a problem compared to last summer because last year the weather was very hot," said another. "Chocolate demand is better this summer."
A resumption of production at a Mars grinding plant following a shutdown for renewal last year could have aided the increase in output, they said.
The UK's Biscuit, Cake, Chocolate and Confectionary Alliance (BCCCA) is expected to release the July-September 1996 grind data by the second week of October.
But commodity broker GNI Ltd said forecasts of a 10 percent increase could prove optimistic.
"We predict that grindings will only be around the 34,000 to 34,500 tonne level -- unchanged from quarter three 1995," it said in a daily report.
"If they exceed this level (particularly after a 26 percent jump in grinds in the second quarter) then it would be very positive," it added.
"Projections are however very dodgy because of plant closures last year," GNI said.
Traders have said the 26 percent jump in the second quarter over the same 1995 period was not exceptional since the Mars plant was shut in 1995.
